assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies is a rare chain from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), its receptor biology) to drugs that have changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality, clarity and clinical and societal impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: The decisive basic contributions come from Holst (physiology and identification of the active GLP-1 forms), Mojsov (peptide chemistry and identification of the active fragment) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and translation). Knudsen led the industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, which is important but arguably more a drug-development contribution. Credit among the basic and translational contributors is contested and the three-person cap forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large randomized outcome trials make the interpretation stable. Recognition is timely, and arguably overdue given the scale of use.
uncertainties: Allocation between Mojsov, Holst and Drucker, and whether Knudsen belongs, is genuinely disputed and I rely on my recollection of the history.
Whether the committee prefers a basic-science or a drug-development framing is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with synthetic receptors turned adoptive immunotherapy into a reproducible treatment for B-cell malignancies, with durable remissions in refractory disease. It is a clear conceptual advance combining receptor engineering, costimulation and manufacturing, with expanding impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the decisive preclinical and clinical development of second-generation CD19 CARs. Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. The original chimeric receptor concept from Eshhar is not among the credited names, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, long follow-up and independent confirmation exist. Limitations in solid tumours, toxicity and secondary malignancy signals are ongoing, but the core B-cell result is mature.
uncertainties: The omission of the original chimeric receptor concept from the credited names weakens the attribution.
I have not verified details of long-term safety data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided genetically targeted, millisecond-precision control of cell activity with light, built on microbial rhodopsins. It transformed neuroscience and physiology as a general method and has begun to reach clinical applications such as vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) showed that channelrhodopsin is a light-gated cation channel. Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control, and Deisseroth developed widely used tools and applications. Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation is also relevant. Six credited people mean any three-person prize leaves out decisive contributors, notably Bamberg.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for roughly two decades across fields. Recognition is timely, with the main difficulty being attribution rather than evidence.
uncertainties: Allocation among six contributors is unresolved and a prize cannot reflect all of them.
Methods may be weighed against discoveries about physiology in the committee's framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV produced a prevention of cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population data showing striking reductions in infection and high-grade lesions. The concept and the impact are clear and of exceptional public health importance.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller established that L1 capsid proteins self-assemble into immunogenic VLPs. Frazer contributed to the early VLP work and to the vaccine's development. Other groups, including Zhou, Kirnbauer and others, also contributed to the early VLP findings, which complicates credit. The three-name set is reasonable but not undisputed.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data from multiple countries are mature and independently confirmed. Zur Hausen was already recognized in 2008 for HPV and cervical cancer, which affects the framing but not the merit.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over early VLP work and the relative role of Frazer are not fully resolved in my knowledge.
Some may see the topic as partly covered by the 2008 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of intracellular signalling from the ER to the nucleus, with IRE1, HAC1 splicing and ATF6 pathways, and has deep implications for secretory-pathway biology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is original, mechanistically clean and conceptually broad.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures: Walter's IRE1 and HAC1 work in yeast and Mori's identification of the UPR pathway in yeast and mammals. A clear two-person configuration is available, though Ron's work on PERK and the integrated stress response is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Core mechanisms have been confirmed in many labs for 30 years. Clinical translation is still emerging, so the recognition rests on basic science.
uncertainties: Contributions from other groups on the mammalian arms are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib was the first demonstration that a rationally targeted kinase inhibitor can transform a fatal cancer into a manageable chronic condition. It established the paradigm of targeted therapy with a clear molecular cause.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the medicinal chemistry programme, Druker the preclinical and clinical proof, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation drugs. Rowley, Witte and others made earlier discoveries about the Philadelphia chromosome and ABL, which are outside the list. The three-person configuration looks fair though Lydon's inclusion is debated against Sawyers's.
assessment.maturity: Decades of survival data and widespread confirmation. Many consider it among the most obvious clinical omissions, and Lasker recognition occurred in 2009.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the basic oncogene work as the true discovery and imatinib as a derivative.
Relative weight of Sawyers versus the earlier chemistry contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING identified how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity through cyclic GMP-AMP, connecting infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumour immunity. It is a conceptually clean mechanistic discovery that reshaped innate immunology.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, while Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. Sun and Wu were first authors in Chen's laboratory. A two-person prize with Chen and Barber is plausible but leaves out Ishikawa, who co-discovered STING.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated with numerous follow-up studies, though therapeutic translation is still early and clinical agonists and antagonists have not yet produced approved drugs.
uncertainties: Credit for STING between Barber and Ishikawa is unsettled.
Possibly premature relative to the clinical impact of other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR signalling revealed the central kinase that couples nutrient and growth-factor signals to cell growth and metabolism, with implications for cancer, ageing, immunity and transplantation through rapamycin-class drugs. The finding is fundamental and conceptually influential.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR in yeast and showed it mediates rapamycin's effects, which is the decisive step. Sabatini identified mTOR and the nutrient-sensing pathways in mammals, though his standing is complicated by past institutional controversy. Schreiber contributed to the rapamycin target-binding discovery with FKBP. Hall alone is a defensible choice, and I name Hall and Sabatini as a pair.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and replicated, with clinical use of rapalogs. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Sabatini's inclusion may be affected by non-scientific considerations that I cannot assess here.
Attribution to the earlier rapamycin and Heitman, Hall and Movva work is complex.
